report.incidentSummary: Starting at approximately 14:20 IST (08:50 UTC) on 2026-09-25, users reported that the AI assistant claimed they held no mutual funds or stocks, while their Portfolio screen displayed correct holdings. Investigation revealed that user-context-service encountered transient context build timeouts (1200ms) between 08:50 UTC and 09:22 UTC due to pod unreadiness. During these timeouts, user-context-service fell back to writing empty context payloads (holdings=0, sips=0) into the shared cache with an excessively long 6-hour TTL (21600s). Consequently, assistant-orchestrator persistently retrieved cached zero-holdings contexts for affected users, sustaining an elevated missing_context_rate (~8%) even after user-context-service errors returned to baseline.
report.rootCauseStatement: During a transient pod unreadiness and timeout spike in user-context-service between 08:50 and 09:22 UTC, timeout handling logic wrote empty fallback user context records ('holdings=0 sips=0') into cache with an excessive 6-hour TTL (21600s). The assistant continuously served cached zero holdings from these poisoned entries, explaining why the symptom persisted after service health recovered and why the independent portfolio-service screen remained unaffected.

hypotheses.cause: During transient request timeouts, user-context-service wrote fallback empty context records (holdings=0, sips=0) into cache with an excessive 6-hour TTL (21600s), causing assistant-orchestrator to persistently read zero holdings for affected users even after the underlying timeout spike resolved.
hypotheses.rationale: Logs directly show user-context-service writing 'holdings=0 sips=0 ttl=21600s (fallback after timeout)' to cache upon timing out after 1200ms. Metrics show that while user-context-service error rate recovered at 09:25 UTC, missing_context_rate remained elevated at ~8% and cache hit rates on the user_context keyspace rose to >98.8% through 11:45 UTC.

hypotheses.cause: user-context-service experienced severe capacity degradation and pod unreadiness between 08:50 and 09:22 UTC, causing context building to exceed the 1200ms timeout threshold for incoming assistant requests.
hypotheses.rationale: Pod unreadiness triggers the initial timeouts ('# of # pods ready' in logs), but capacity saturation alone contradicts the persistent symptom past 09:25 UTC when pod error rates returned to baseline while missing context remained high.

hypotheses.cause: Upstream latency or degradation in portfolio-service prevented user-context-service from retrieving holdings within its timeout window.
hypotheses.rationale: portfolio-service maintained a steady ~0.20% error rate, ~134ms p95 latency, and served holdings requests normally throughout the entire window.

facts.statement: user-context-service error rate spiked from ~0.30% to 6.31% at 08:50 UTC, peaked at 10.32% at 09:05 UTC, and returned to baseline (~0.27%) by 09:25 UTC.
user-context-service missing_context_rate jumped from ~0.8% to 12.00% at 08:50 UTC, peaked at 20.46% at 09:05 UTC, and remained elevated between 7.06% and 8.66% through 11:45 UTC.
assistant-orchestrator error rate stayed steady between 0.38% and 0.57% across the entire investigation window.
Between 08:50:18 UTC and 09:21:57 UTC, user-context-service logged 193 instances of 'context build timed out after 1200ms (holdings fetch pending); # of # pods ready'.
On context build timeout, user-context-service logged WARN entries writing fallback empty context to cache: 'cache SET user_ctx:<uid> holdings=0 sips=0 ttl=21600s (fallback after timeout)'.
Cache hit rate for the user_context keyspace increased from ~94.8% up to 98.8%-99.2% starting at ~09:00 UTC, while other keyspaces remained stable at ~94%.
portfolio-service p95 latency remained between 118ms and 152ms and error rate remained flat at ~0.20% with normal request rates and logs.
No deployments or configuration changes were executed on assistant-orchestrator, user-context-service, portfolio-service, or cache on 2026-09-25 leading up to 08:50 UTC.

inferences.statement: The ongoing failure of the assistant to report holdings past 09:25 UTC is driven by cache poisoning: empty context records with a 6-hour TTL (21600s) are served on cache hits instead of querying live data.
portfolio-service did not cause the context build timeouts, as its error rate and p95 latency were completely normal and within its 1000ms upstream limit.
The context timeouts in user-context-service were triggered by internal pod unreadiness or container concurrency saturation rather than an external dependency failure.

assumptions.statement: assistant-orchestrator relies entirely on user-context-service cache payloads and does not perform secondary validation or bypass cache when holdings count is zero.

timeline.event: knowledge-index deployed CHG-48223 (v1.8.0 -> v1.9.0); baseline user-context-service error rate is ~0.30% and missing_context_rate is ~0.84%.

user-context-service begins logging context build timeouts and setting empty context in cache: 'cache SET user_ctx:u_67605287 holdings=0 sips=0 ttl=21600s (fallback after timeout)'. Error rate rises to 6.31%.
user-context-service error rate peaks at 10.32% and missing_context_rate peaks at 20.46%.
Last timeout log entry recorded in user-context-service; pods return to ready status.
user-context-service error rate returns to normal baseline (~0.27%), but missing_context_rate persists elevated at ~8.5% due to 6-hour cached fallback records.
Support team lead files incident INC-3320 as assistant continues answering that affected users have no holdings.

confidence.rationale: Direct log records capture the exact fallback write of 'holdings=0 sips=0' with 21600s TTL upon timeout, perfectly matching the persistent ~8% missing context rate and elevated cache hit rate through the rest of the window.

gaps.description: Infrastructure logs and Kubernetes metrics explaining why user-context-service pods became unready between 08:50 UTC and 09:22 UTC were not retrieved due to tool budget limits.
gaps.impact: The exact trigger of the initial transient pod unreadiness is unconfirmed, though its impact and the failure-handling mechanism are fully established.

recommendedActions.action: Invalidate or flush keys matching 'user_ctx:*' with 'holdings=0' in the shared cache, or execute a targeted cache purge for users affected between 08:50 and 09:25 UTC.
recommendedActions.rationale: Removes poisoned fallback context records with 6-hour TTL, allowing assistant-orchestrator to fetch fresh, accurate holdings immediately.
recommendedActions.verification: Check that user-context-service missing_context_rate metric drops from ~8% back to baseline (~0.8%).

recommendedActions.action: Modify fallback caching logic in user-context-service to either not cache fallback empty contexts or cache them with a short TTL (e.g., 30-60 seconds) rather than 21600s.
recommendedActions.rationale: Prevents transient downstream or pod readiness hiccups from poisoning user contexts for hours.
recommendedActions.verification: Inspect code diff and verify in staging that synthetic context timeouts do not set a 21600s TTL on empty fallback entries.

recommendedActions.action: Investigate the Kubernetes pod unreadiness events and container resource limits for user-context-service during 08:50-09:22 UTC.
recommendedActions.rationale: Identifies why pods experienced readiness dropouts under normal traffic.
recommendedActions.verification: Review Kubernetes event logs and pod CPU/memory utilization metrics around 08:50 UTC.

report.justification: Although the investigation completed without formal critic review, conclusive outcome is warranted because log evidence directly captures user-context-service executing fallback cache writes of zero holdings with a 21600s (6-hour) TTL during the 08:50-09:22 UTC timeout window. This directly and fully accounts for both the ongoing symptom and the divergent missing_context_rate metric remaining at ~8% after error rate returned to normal.

payload.markdown:
# Investigation report: Assistant cannot see user holdings

**Outcome:** conclusive · **Stop reason:** completed · **Confidence:** 0.90 · **Written by:** reporting agent

## Summary
Starting at approximately 14:20 IST (08:50 UTC) on 2026-09-25, users reported that the AI assistant claimed they held no mutual funds or stocks, while their Portfolio screen displayed correct holdings. Investigation revealed that user-context-service encountered transient context build timeouts (1200ms) between 08:50 UTC and 09:22 UTC due to pod unreadiness. During these timeouts, user-context-service fell back to writing empty context payloads (holdings=0, sips=0) into the shared cache with an excessively long 6-hour TTL (21600s). Consequently, assistant-orchestrator persistently retrieved cached zero-holdings contexts for affected users, sustaining an elevated missing_context_rate (~8%) even after user-context-service errors returned to baseline.

**Root cause:** During a transient pod unreadiness and timeout spike in user-context-service between 08:50 and 09:22 UTC, timeout handling logic wrote empty fallback user context records ('holdings=0 sips=0') into cache with an excessive 6-hour TTL (21600s). The assistant continuously served cached zero holdings from these poisoned entries, explaining why the symptom persisted after service health recovered and why the independent portfolio-service screen remained unaffected.

## Hypotheses
1. **During transient request timeouts, user-context-service wrote fallback empty context records (holdings=0, sips=0) into cache with an excessive 6-hour TTL (21600s), causing assistant-orchestrator to persistently read zero holdings for affected users even after the underlying timeout spike resolved.** — `user-context-service`, cache_or_staleness, confidence 0.90, supported
   - Supporting: [ev_1, ev_2, ev_7, ev_12, ev_16] · Contradicting: none
   - Logs directly show user-context-service writing 'holdings=0 sips=0 ttl=21600s (fallback after timeout)' to cache upon timing out after 1200ms. Metrics show that while user-context-service error rate recovered at 09:25 UTC, missing_context_rate remained elevated at ~8% and cache hit rates on the user_context keyspace rose to >98.8% through 11:45 UTC.
2. **user-context-service experienced severe capacity degradation and pod unreadiness between 08:50 and 09:22 UTC, causing context building to exceed the 1200ms timeout threshold for incoming assistant requests.** — `user-context-service`, capacity_saturation, confidence 0.65, supported
   - Supporting: [ev_1, ev_12, ev_16] · Contradicting: [ev_2]
   - Pod unreadiness triggers the initial timeouts ('# of # pods ready' in logs), but capacity saturation alone contradicts the persistent symptom past 09:25 UTC when pod error rates returned to baseline while missing context remained high.
3. **Upstream latency or degradation in portfolio-service prevented user-context-service from retrieving holdings within its timeout window.** — `portfolio-service`, upstream_dependency_degradation, confidence 0.05, ruled_out
   - Supporting: none · Contradicting: [ev_8, ev_9, ev_10, ev_14, ev_15]
   - portfolio-service maintained a steady ~0.20% error rate, ~134ms p95 latency, and served holdings requests normally throughout the entire window.

## Facts
- user-context-service error rate spiked from ~0.30% to 6.31% at 08:50 UTC, peaked at 10.32% at 09:05 UTC, and returned to baseline (~0.27%) by 09:25 UTC. [ev_1]
- user-context-service missing_context_rate jumped from ~0.8% to 12.00% at 08:50 UTC, peaked at 20.46% at 09:05 UTC, and remained elevated between 7.06% and 8.66% through 11:45 UTC. [ev_2]
- assistant-orchestrator error rate stayed steady between 0.38% and 0.57% across the entire investigation window. [ev_3]
- Between 08:50:18 UTC and 09:21:57 UTC, user-context-service logged 193 instances of 'context build timed out after 1200ms (holdings fetch pending); # of # pods ready'. [ev_12]
- On context build timeout, user-context-service logged WARN entries writing fallback empty context to cache: 'cache SET user_ctx:<uid> holdings=0 sips=0 ttl=21600s (fallback after timeout)'. [ev_12, ev_16]
- Cache hit rate for the user_context keyspace increased from ~94.8% up to 98.8%-99.2% starting at ~09:00 UTC, while other keyspaces remained stable at ~94%. [ev_7]
- portfolio-service p95 latency remained between 118ms and 152ms and error rate remained flat at ~0.20% with normal request rates and logs. [ev_8, ev_9, ev_10, ev_14, ev_15]
- No deployments or configuration changes were executed on assistant-orchestrator, user-context-service, portfolio-service, or cache on 2026-09-25 leading up to 08:50 UTC. [ev_6]

## Inferences
- The ongoing failure of the assistant to report holdings past 09:25 UTC is driven by cache poisoning: empty context records with a 6-hour TTL (21600s) are served on cache hits instead of querying live data. [ev_2, ev_7, ev_12, ev_16]
- portfolio-service did not cause the context build timeouts, as its error rate and p95 latency were completely normal and within its 1000ms upstream limit. [ev_8, ev_9, ev_13, ev_14]
- The context timeouts in user-context-service were triggered by internal pod unreadiness or container concurrency saturation rather than an external dependency failure. [ev_1, ev_12]

## Assumptions
- assistant-orchestrator relies entirely on user-context-service cache payloads and does not perform secondary validation or bypass cache when holdings count is zero.

## Timeline
- **2026-09-25T08:45:00.000Z (14:15 IST)** knowledge-index deployed CHG-48223 (v1.8.0 -> v1.9.0); baseline user-context-service error rate is ~0.30% and missing_context_rate is ~0.84%. [ev_1, ev_2, ev_11]
- **2026-09-25T08:50:03.000Z (14:20 IST)** user-context-service begins logging context build timeouts and setting empty context in cache: 'cache SET user_ctx:u_67605287 holdings=0 sips=0 ttl=21600s (fallback after timeout)'. Error rate rises to 6.31%. [ev_1, ev_12, ev_16]
- **2026-09-25T09:05:00.000Z (14:35 IST)** user-context-service error rate peaks at 10.32% and missing_context_rate peaks at 20.46%. [ev_1, ev_2]
- **2026-09-25T09:21:57.000Z (14:51 IST)** Last timeout log entry recorded in user-context-service; pods return to ready status. [ev_12]
- **2026-09-25T09:25:00.000Z (14:55 IST)** user-context-service error rate returns to normal baseline (~0.27%), but missing_context_rate persists elevated at ~8.5% due to 6-hour cached fallback records. [ev_1, ev_2, ev_7]
- **2026-09-25T11:00:00.000Z (16:30 IST)** Support team lead files incident INC-3320 as assistant continues answering that affected users have no holdings. [ev_2]

## Confidence
0.90: Direct log records capture the exact fallback write of 'holdings=0 sips=0' with 21600s TTL upon timeout, perfectly matching the persistent ~8% missing context rate and elevated cache hit rate through the rest of the window.

## Gaps
- Infrastructure logs and Kubernetes metrics explaining why user-context-service pods became unready between 08:50 UTC and 09:22 UTC were not retrieved due to tool budget limits. (impact: The exact trigger of the initial transient pod unreadiness is unconfirmed, though its impact and the failure-handling mechanism are fully established.)

## Recommended actions (not executed)
- **[now]** Invalidate or flush keys matching 'user_ctx:*' with 'holdings=0' in the shared cache, or execute a targeted cache purge for users affected between 08:50 and 09:25 UTC. [ev_2, ev_7, ev_12, ev_16]
  - Why: Removes poisoned fallback context records with 6-hour TTL, allowing assistant-orchestrator to fetch fresh, accurate holdings immediately.
  - Verify: Check that user-context-service missing_context_rate metric drops from ~8% back to baseline (~0.8%).
- **[next]** Modify fallback caching logic in user-context-service to either not cache fallback empty contexts or cache them with a short TTL (e.g., 30-60 seconds) rather than 21600s. [ev_12, ev_16]
  - Why: Prevents transient downstream or pod readiness hiccups from poisoning user contexts for hours.
  - Verify: Inspect code diff and verify in staging that synthetic context timeouts do not set a 21600s TTL on empty fallback entries.
- **[later]** Investigate the Kubernetes pod unreadiness events and container resource limits for user-context-service during 08:50-09:22 UTC. [ev_1, ev_12]
  - Why: Identifies why pods experienced readiness dropouts under normal traffic.
  - Verify: Review Kubernetes event logs and pod CPU/memory utilization metrics around 08:50 UTC.
